Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the order form and legal asked us to propose one commercial tweak before signature: a temporary monthly "buffer" we can draw against when usage dips below the commit during the first 12 months, instead of immediate true-up charges. The idea is a 10% drawdown pool that resets quarterly unless used.

Can Redwood:
- Add a short paragraph in Exhibit B that allows a quarterly buffer drawdown of up to 10% of committed units?
- Confirm whether drawing against the buffer delays true-up invoices or simply offsets them?
- Confirm any cap on total drawdown across the contract term.

We attached a suggested redline (Novus_Orderform_Redline_v1.pdf) — please confirm feasibility from your side (billing / legal). If not feasible, a short limited credit (one-time cushion) would be our fallback.

Appreciate a quick read — we are targeting signature week of Aug 6.

Best,
Helene
Director, Procurement
Novus Health

Hi Helene — thanks for the clear ask and the suggested language. Quick answers up front:
- We can support a temporary drawdown mechanism but want to align on billing treatment and operational constraints.
- If the buffer is used, it would offset invoiced usage in the quarter (i.e., reduce billed units) rather than technically pausing the true-up calculation — functionally similar to a credit.
- We prefer a capped cumulative drawdown (e.g., no more than 25% of one year’s commit over the contract term) to protect capacity planning for Dedicated pools.

Looping in Ben (AE) and Legal for redline review. Marissa: I’ve attached Novus’s marked copy (they sent v1). Can you review Exhibit B and the order schedule for any legal or risk blockers? Ben / Rishi — heads up on the proposed cumulative cap.

I can host a quick 30-min alignment call tomorrow if useful.

Thanks,
Mina

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Novus’s ask. Client wants a 10% quarterly buffer that rolls and can be drawn against instead of immediate true-up billing for dips in usage. They’re open to a capped cumulative drawdown.

Commercial considerations:
- Protecting the Dedicated capacity / reserved slots is important for us; if they use buffer frequently it undermines provisioning economics.
- Finance preference would be a credit offset against invoices (reduces revenue recognized immediately) vs delaying invoice generation.

Marissa — can you:
1) Draft a tight redline for Exhibit B that:
   - Defines the buffer, reset cadence, and cumulative cap (we suggested 25% of one year’s commit);
   - Specifies billing treatment: buffer as a credit applied to the invoice covering the quarter in which draw occurred;
   - Includes a fall-through where excessive use triggers a review / possible commit increase.
2) Flag any legal risk (SLA, capacity guarantees, auditability).

Rishi — if we accept 25% cumulative cap and credits applied quarterly, what’s the P&L impact estimate for first-year revenue recognition? Rough ballpark is fine for the call.

Appreciate quick turnaround — client hopes to sign early August.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Order form draft — guardrails and smoothing question

Thanks Ben — draft redline below and key legal notes. I also attached a clean PDF v3 that incorporates the markup.

Key legal approach (summary):
- We can accept a limited drawdown buffer but must limit operational exposure. Propose: 10% quarterly buffer that resets at quarter end; cumulative usage of buffer capped at 25% of the annual committed units across the first 12 months.
- Billing: buffer usage is recorded as a credit applied to the invoice for the quarter in which usage occurred. This preserves billing cadence and audit trail (we’ll document usage on the monthly usage report).
- Trigger: if buffer usage exceeds the cumulative cap, Redwood may require the customer to either (a) increase committed units for the remainder of the term or (b) convert future usage to overage billing at list rates and true-up for past shortfalls.
- Operational clause: customer must provide 14 days’ advance notice if they expect to draw more than 50% of the available buffer in a given quarter (helps capacity planning).
- Audit & logs: include reference to usage reports and audit rights limited to verifying buffer draws (no broad data access).

Legal redline notes:
1) Remove ambiguous language like "delay true-ups" — instead use concrete billing mechanics (credit offset).
2) Add a definition section in Exhibit B for "Buffer Units", "Cumulative Buffer Cap" and "Reset Date".
3) Add a short fall-through remedy (we can offer an explicit 30-day cure / commit increase window).

I don’t see a regulatory blocker; main risk is potential capacity misalignment for Dedicated pools if client constantly dips and uses the buffer. Recommend acceptance with the proposed cumulative cap and the 14-day notice.

I’ll circulate DocuSign-ready files once Ben confirms the commercial cap and Rishi gives a quick P&L ballpark.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Attachment: Novus_Orderform_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf stub)
